slides.headline: The Man China Just Honored Starved Millions
slides.body: Fifty years after his death, crowds still lay flowers for Mao. Beijing has never confirmed how many the famine killed.

slides.headline: 1958: Mao Promised to Out-Produce Britain
slides.body: Mao launched the Great Leap Forward, forcing peasants into communes to hit impossible steel and grain quotas overnight.

slides.headline: Officials Lied About Harvests to Survive
slides.body: Local cadres reported fictional bumper crops. Beijing seized the grain anyway and shipped it abroad while villages starved.

slides.headline: 36 Million Dead, One Banned Book
slides.body: Journalist Yang Jisheng used sealed party archives to count the dead. China still bans his book, Tombstone.

slides.headline: Every Regime Names a Weather Event
slides.body: States rarely admit what they cause. China called it 'natural disaster.' The Soviets, Cambodia, North Korea wrote the same line.

slides.headline: Beijing Has Never Published a Number
slides.body: Fifty years of flowers at his statue. Zero years of an official death toll. Which one erases the other?
